description:
MEASURED 2026-08-13 against ENDF/B-VIII.0 tsl-crystalline-graphite (MAT=30), found while quantifying temperature-grid thinning. Regression-locked by
tests/thermal_temperature_thinning.rs::production_interpolation_leaves_the_bracket_above_half_an_ev. NOT FIXED --
it needs its own change and its own V&V.

THE DEFECT. sigma_inel(E,T) is monotone in T across the tabulated grid, so an interpolated value at a temperature
between two tabulated ones MUST lie between their two cross sections. The production interpolation does not:

  at 393.15 K, E = 3.9 eV:  interpolated 4.4175 b   against the bracket [4.6097, 4.6367]
                            -- roughly 4-5% BELOW the lower bracketing value, i.e. outside it entirely

Same behaviour at 523.15 K, 900 K and 1400 K. About 1% low at 0.5 eV. CORRECT at and below 0.1 eV.

WHY IT HAS NEVER BEEN CAUGHT. The existing coverage (tests/thermal_graphite_coherent.rs) checks 0.0253 eV only,
which is inside the region where the interpolation behaves. The defect lives above ~0.5 eV.

WHO IT AFFECTS: EVERY non-tabulated temperature request today. The graphite evaluation tabulates 296, 400, 500, 600,
700, 800, 1000, 1200, 1600, 2000 K; the IAEA HTR-10 B1-B4 benchmarks are at 293.15 / 393.15 / 523.15 K, all of which
are interpolated. So this is on the HTR-10 critical path, not a corner case.

SEVERITY IN CONTEXT: at 0.0253 eV, where the thermal spectrum lives, the interpolation is fine, and coherent elastic
(~90% of the thermal cross section) is unaffected. The error is in the epithermal tail of the inelastic channel. It
is a real defect and a bounded one -- do not report it as breaking the thermal spectrum without measuring that.

NOT THE CAUSE, already ruled out by the reporting agent: zero-endpoint handling. A PreserveZeros variant gave
bit-identical statistics, and the reconstruction was verified monotone. What was NOT established is why ln S is so
non-linear in T in the far tail -- only that it is. Start there.

RELATED: op-cjw.22 (inelastic temperature interpolation) is filed P4 on the stated assumption that target temps are
tabulated exactly. That assumption fails for HTR-10, and this bead is direct evidence the interpolation it defers is
actually wrong rather than merely absent. Consider re-prioritising or merging.

Also fixed in passing while measuring this, and worth knowing: IncoherentInelastic was DISCARDING the inelastic LI
temperature-interpolation codes -- the same class of defect as op-1y4y on the elastic side. mf7.rs now retains them
(IncoherentInelastic::temp_interp), so the tape's own LI=4 is read rather than assumed.
title: njoy THERMR DEFECT: inelastic temperature interpolation leaves its tabulated bracket above ~0.5 eV (4-5% low at 3.9 eV)

description:
Prophylactic, from the op-hc2o post-mortem (2026-08-14).

Two defects in that bead's step 5 were the SAME class of failure: physics that is implemented, tested at unit level, and then never actually invoked by the path that matters.

- Nuclide::sample_thermal was implemented, had 7 green V&V tests at nuclide level, and had exactly ONE caller in the crate (physics::transport_csg). Both k-eigenvalue paths -- physics::keff and pebble_beds::keff_delta -- silently fell through to free-gas kinematics for 3.5 months.
- The one test that would have caught it was #[ignore]d for a reason that was itself wrong (a nuclide NAMING error, "C12" vs the real "C0", misdiagnosed as a missing-data gap and attributed to a bead that was never even filed).

Neither showed up as a failure. Everything was green the whole time.

WHAT TO ADD:
1. A test that asserts every collision path routes thermal scattering. Concretely: for each of the transport entry points (run_keff, run_keff_delta, transport_csg), run a short fixed case with a moderator nuclide carrying an S(alpha,beta) table and assert the result DIFFERS from the same case without it. A bit-identical result is the exact signature of a dead branch and is trivially detectable -- that is what caught this one.
2. A guard against silently-ignored tests. #[ignore] on a V&V test hid a defect for months. Options: a periodic '--ignored' sweep in the suite runner, or a rule that an #[ignore] reason naming a bead must reference a bead that EXISTS (op-wqk.21 did not).
3. Consider a general audit for other implemented-but-uncalled physics. grep for pub fns in src/physics/ and src/material/ whose only callers are tests. sample_thermal would have shown up.

Not urgent, but this class of bug is invisible to the existing gates by construction, and the workspace has now been bitten by it once at P1 severity on the HTR-10 critical path.
title: outram-mc: no regression gate stops a thermal-scattering law from being wired with no caller

description:
IAPWS-IF97 Region 5 requires explicit backward equations to compute temperature from pressure and enthalpy, and from pressure and entropy. These equations are currently missing from tampines-steam-tables. This issue also covers a related explicit near-critical Region 4 (h,s) flash, to replace the iterative pressure fallback near the critical point.

Scope:
1. Region 5 backward equations - T(p,h) and T(p,s) for high-temperature water/steam.
2. Region 4 near-critical (h,s) flash - explicit p(h,s), Tsat(p), and vapor-quality x(h,s) for 623.15 <= Tsat <= 647.04 K, replacing the iterative pressure-fallback path in that near-critical band.

Three prototypes (ChatGPT/NUS ChatGPT Edu-assisted) posted as comments on GitHub issue #34:
- Python prototype: Region 5 forward equations + T_ph_5/T_ps_5 Chebyshev fit + validate() routine
- region5_backward_explicit.rs: direct Rust transcription of the Region 5 backward fit
- region4_hs_nearcritical_explicit.rs: p_hs_4_nearcritical, tsat_p_4, x_hs_4_nearcritical

Fit domains:
- Region 5: 1e-4 <= p <= 50 MPa, 1073.15 <= T <= 2273.15 K
- Region 4 near-critical: 623.15 <= Tsat <= 647.04 K

Not an official IAPWS supplementary release - needs review, integration into the Rust crate, and independent validation against IAPWS-IF97 reference data before it can be trusted.

Follow-up work:
- Port the fitted Chebyshev coefficients / evaluation logic into crates/tampines-steam-tables as Rust
- Add unit tests validating against forward equations and published IAPWS-IF97 reference data where available
- Document methodology + results per the workspace V&V documentation rule

GitHub issue: https://github.com/theodoreOnzGit/outram-park-backend/issues/34
title: Tampines steam tables: explicit backward equations — Region 5 T(p,h)/T(p,s) and Region 4 near-critical (h,s) flash
